title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 1.1 sets up the Tannakian description of Hodge structures with G-symmetry. G is an algebraic group over Q.

(1) The torus. S = Res_{C/R} G_m (written as a product over C/R of G_{m,C}), so S(R) = C*. U ⊂ S is the kernel of the norm S → G_{m,R}, the circle group.

(2) Representations of S. Rep_R(S) is equivalent to the category of real vector spaces V_R with a bigrading V_C = ⊕ V^{p,q} satisfying V^{p,q} = conj(V^{q,p}). This is a 'Hodge prestructure': a real Hodge structure without any weight condition. The NB fixes the convention that λ ∈ C* acts on V^{p,q} by λ^p λ̄^q. The canonical embedding G_{m,R} → S corresponds to the total grading: R* acts on V^{p,q} by λ^{p+q}.

(3) Tannakian step. Consider the fibre functor Rep(G) → Modf(Q) → Modf(R) → Modf(C) (forget, then extend scalars). Suppose we are given, on this composite, a bigrading with the conjugation symmetry that is functorial in Rep(G) and compatible with the Q-structure. That is, a functorial Hodge prestructure on every representation, compatible with ⊗. Such data is equivalent to a homomorphism j: S → G_R. This is Tannaka duality: ⊗-automorphisms of the fibre functor are G, so a ⊗-compatible S-action on the fibre functor is a homomorphism S → G_R.

(4) Weight. Next, give a central homomorphism w: G_m → G over Q, i.e. a Q-rational grading V = ⊕ V^n of the forgetful functor by subrepresentations. One imposes V^n_C = ⊕_{p+q=n} V^{p,q}. The next page shows this amounts to j restricted to G_{m,R} being w_R. That page then:
- fixes a character ε: G → G_m giving the Tate object;
- requires ε∘j = Norm, i.e. 'Q(1)' of bidegree (1,1);
- characterises polarizations φ: V×V → Q(-p) by positivity of φ_R(x, Cy).

In modern terms this is the Deligne torus, Hodge structures as S-representations, a Mumford–Tate-type homomorphism h: S → G_R with a rational central weight cocharacter, and Tannakian families of Hodge structures. It is essentially the data later packaged as Shimura data and as 'Hodge structures on a Tannakian category' (Saavedra Rivano). The goal is to define Hodge realizations and polarizations on representations of a motivic Galois group.
errors: No genuine mathematical error. The sign convention (λ acts on V^{p,q} by λ^p λ̄^q) is opposite to Deligne's later convention (λ^{-p} λ̄^{-q}). Correspondingly the next page's 'Q(1) of bidegree (1,1)' is what is now usually written Q(-1); this is consistent internally.

Centrality of w is bracketed. Any cocharacter G_m → G gives a grading of the fibre functor. Centrality (defined over Q) is exactly what makes the grading functorial by subobjects of Rep(G), i.e. a grading of the category. The page does not spell this out, but the bracketed insertion shows awareness.

ideas.what: S = Res_{C/R} G_m with S(R) = C*, and U = ker(Norm) as the circle subgroup
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Théorie de Hodge II, 1971; Travaux de Shimura, 1971)
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's published texts to my knowledge; appears in Saavedra Rivano, Catégories tannakiennes (1972), derived from Grothendieck's programme

ideas.what: Real Hodge (pre)structures are the same as real representations of S, with λ acting by λ^p λ̄^q on V^{p,q}, and G_{m,R} ⊂ S giving the weight grading
ideas.modern_name: Hodge structures as representations of the Deligne torus
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1971); Mumford 1966 used the circle U

ideas.what: A ⊗-functorial Hodge prestructure on the fibre functor of Rep(G) is equivalent to a homomorphism S → G_R
ideas.modern_name: Tannakian description of variations/families of Hodge structures; Mumford–Tate homomorphism h
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (1972), Deligne (1979 Variétés de Shimura), Deligne–Milne (1982)
ideas.where_published: Saavedra Rivano 1972 Ch. V–VI (thesis under Grothendieck)

ideas.what: Rational central weight cocharacter w: G_m → G with h|G_{m,R} = w_R; Tate character ε with ε∘h = Norm; polarization via positivity of φ(x, Cy)
ideas.modern_name: Weight homomorphism and Tate character in Shimura data / motivic Galois groups; Hodge–Riemann polarization condition

missed.claim: If the notes really date from around 1965, they contain the Deligne torus formalism several years before Deligne's 1971 publications. This includes the circle U, h: S → G_R, a central rational weight cocharacter, and a Tate character with ε∘h = Norm. This is historical priority evidence: Grothendieck had the standard Shimura-datum / Mumford–Tate packaging (minus the axioms on ad h) in his motivic Galois group programme, and the attribution usually goes to Deligne.
missed.quote: La donnée sur le foncteur composé d'une bigraduation ... équivaut : à la donnée d'un hom S → G_R
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This clarifies the genealogy of Hodge structures as S-representations and of Shimura data. It credits Grothendieck's 1960s Tannakian motivic programme as the source, not only Saavedra and Deligne. The dating is uncertain ('s.d.'), so this must be checked.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is now standard. What is notable is its possible early date and that the attribution in the literature is to Deligne and Saavedra. Since the notes are undated and Grothendieck's influence on Saavedra is known, the surprise is moderate.
transcription_corrections: The homomorphism S → G_R is labelled 'j' in the image (consistent with the next page), not 'h'.
The homomorphism G_m → G is labelled 'i' in the image ('i: G_m → G'), not 'w'. The next page's 'j|G_mR = i_R' confirms this.
'Rep(𝕊)' and '𝕊' are written with a stylised $-like symbol for the Deligne torus.
'dans la condition' is possibly 'd'où la condition' (handwriting ambiguous).
